questions.question: A movement performed entirely by an external force with no voluntary muscle contraction by the patient is:
questions.explanation: Passive movements maintain joint range and soft tissue extensibility when the patient cannot move; they do not strengthen muscles.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: An active-assisted exercise is used when the muscle:

options.C: Can contract but cannot complete the range without help (about grade 2 or below against gravity)

questions.explanation: The patient contributes and the therapist, a pulley or the opposite limb supplies the extra force.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Free (active) exercises are movements:

options.B: Performed by the patient's own muscles without external resistance, assistance or apparatus loading

questions.explanation: Free exercises are classified as local or general and include mobilising, strengthening and coordination exercises.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which exercise requires the muscle to work against an external force such as weights, springs or the therapist's hands?
questions.explanation: Resistance increases the load for strengthening: manual, mechanical, isotonic, isometric or isokinetic.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: An isometric contraction is one in which:

options.A: Speed is kept constant by a dynamometer
options.B: The muscle shortens against constant resistance
options.D: Muscle tension develops without a change in muscle length or joint movement

questions.explanation: Isometrics are valuable early after injury or surgery; strength gains are specific to the joint angle (±10°).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In an eccentric contraction the muscle:

options.B: Lengthens while producing tension to control a load

questions.explanation: Examples: lowering a weight, descending stairs. Eccentric work produces higher force with lower energy cost and causes more delayed-onset muscle soreness.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In isokinetic exercise:

options.A: Resistance is given only by springs
options.C: Angular velocity is held constant while resistance accommodates to the force applied
options.D: Weight is constant and speed varies

questions.explanation: Isokinetic dynamometers (Cybex, Biodex) allow maximum loading through the whole range at a pre-set speed.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A closed kinetic chain exercise is one in which the distal segment:

options.A: Is fixed or meets resistance, so that movements occur at several joints simultaneously
options.C: Is always supported by a pulley

questions.explanation: Squats and leg press are closed chain; knee extension on a bench is open chain. Closed chain exercises produce less shear on the ACL and more co-contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Plyometric exercise is based on the principle that:

options.A: A rapid eccentric stretch of a muscle before a concentric contraction increases the force of the subsequent contraction
options.C: Resistance should be applied only in one direction
options.D: A slow stretch reduces the stretch reflex

questions.explanation: Stretch–shortening cycle uses elastic energy and the stretch reflex; used in late-stage rehabilitation (jumping, bounding).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The principle of overload in strength training states that:

options.A: Muscle strength improves only when it is stressed beyond its normal level of demand
options.B: Exercise must be done to fatigue daily
options.C: Strength improves with light loading only

questions.explanation: Progressive overload of intensity, volume or frequency is required for adaptation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The SAID principle (Specific Adaptation to Imposed Demands) means that:

options.B: The body adapts specifically to the type of exercise (mode, speed, range) it performs
options.C: Strength gains transfer equally to all movements

questions.explanation: Training should replicate functional demands in contraction type, velocity and joint angle.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A 10-RM refers to the:

options.A: Weight that can be lifted once
options.C: Maximum load a muscle can move through the full range exactly 10 times

questions.explanation: The repetition maximum concept was introduced by DeLorme. 1-RM is the heaviest load for a single full-range repetition.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In DeLorme's progressive resistive exercise regimen, the three sets of ten repetitions are performed at:
questions.explanation: Original DeLorme: 10 reps at 50% of 10-RM, 10 at 75%, 10 at 100%. The Oxford technique reverses the order (100%, 75%, 50%) to account for fatigue.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Oxford technique of progressive resistive exercise differs from DeLorme's in that:

options.A: The lightest set is performed first
options.C: The heaviest set is performed first and the load is reduced in successive sets

questions.explanation: Oxford (Zinovieff): 100%, 75%, 50% of 10-RM so that load decreases as the muscle fatigues.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the first 6–8 weeks of a strength-training programme, the increase in strength is mainly due to:

options.B: Neural adaptations (increased motor unit recruitment and synchronisation)

questions.explanation: Hypertrophy becomes dominant after the first 6–8 weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: To allow adaptation, resistance exercise for the same muscle group is generally performed:

options.D: 2–3 times per week with at least 48 hours between sessions

questions.explanation: Muscle adapts during recovery; ACSM recommends 2–3 days per week for each major muscle group.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The single most important variable in a programme designed to increase muscle strength is:
questions.explanation: Strength gains require a high intensity (70–85% of 1-RM) with low to moderate repetitions; endurance training uses low load and many repetitions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: To improve muscular endurance the best prescription is:

options.A: Low load (about 30–50% of 1-RM) and high repetitions

questions.explanation: Muscular endurance is improved through high repetition, low intensity work that increases oxidative capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: During resistance exercise, patients should be advised to avoid the Valsalva manoeuvre because it:

options.D: Raises intrathoracic pressure and blood pressure while reducing venous return

questions.explanation: Breath-holding is risky in patients with hypertension or cardiac disease; exhale during the effort phase.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) is most associated with:
questions.explanation: Pain peaks at 24–72 hours after eccentric loading due to micro-damage of connective tissue and muscle fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Muscle fatigue is defined as:

options.D: A reduction in the ability of a muscle to generate force after repeated or sustained activity

questions.explanation: Fatigue may be central or peripheral and is reversible with rest.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Static stretching involves:

options.A: Slowly lengthening a muscle to the point of mild discomfort and holding the position

questions.explanation: Holding for 15–30 seconds is effective for most adults; it carries less risk of injury than ballistic stretching.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which statement about ballistic stretching is correct?

options.C: It is the safest method for beginners
options.D: It uses rapid, bouncing movements and may trigger the stretch reflex, increasing injury risk

questions.explanation: Ballistic stretching can cause muscle strain because the stretch reflex resists rapid lengthening.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The physiological basis of hold-relax stretching is:

options.D: Autogenic inhibition via Golgi tendon organs after an isometric contraction

questions.explanation: A maximal isometric contraction of the shortened muscle stimulates GTOs, followed by relaxation and a deeper stretch.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The recommended duration for a static stretch in healthy adults is about:
questions.explanation: Older adults may benefit from 30–60 seconds. Holding longer than 60 seconds provides little additional benefit.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A myostatic contracture is due to:

options.B: Fibrosis of the joint capsule only
options.C: Shortening of the muscle without structural changes in the joint

questions.explanation: Myostatic contractures result from prolonged positioning with the muscle shortened and respond to stretching, whereas pseudomyostatic contractures are due to CNS lesions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Stretching of collagenous tissue is most effective when it is performed:

options.C: With cold tissue and quick force
options.D: After warming the tissue, with a low-load, long-duration stretch

questions.explanation: Heat increases collagen extensibility; low-load prolonged stretch produces plastic (permanent) elongation with less risk of tearing.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Passive insufficiency of a two-joint muscle is demonstrated when:

options.B: A muscle cannot develop tension because it is already shortened
options.D: The muscle is stretched over both joints so that full range at the second joint cannot be achieved (e.g. hamstring tightness limiting hip flexion with knee extended)

questions.explanation: Active insufficiency: the muscle is shortened over both joints and cannot produce force; passive insufficiency: the antagonist is stretched across two joints and limits motion.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A 90–90 test, in which the knee cannot extend beyond about 20° when the hip is flexed to 90°, indicates:
questions.explanation: The 90–90 hamstring length test; popliteal angle >20° indicates shortening.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Jacobson's progressive relaxation technique involves:

options.B: Systematic contraction followed by relaxation of different muscle groups

questions.explanation: The patient learns to recognise the difference between tension and relaxation by alternately contracting and relaxing muscle groups.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Laura Mitchell's physiological relaxation is based on the principle of:

options.D: Reciprocal relaxation: contracting the antagonist to relax the agonist

questions.explanation: Mitchell's method moves joints away from the pattern of tension using the opposite motion, bringing about relaxation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A good starting position for general relaxation in the clinic is:

options.A: Prone with the head rotated fully
options.B: Sitting forward on a hard chair
options.D: Supine or crook lying with support under the head and knees

questions.explanation: Comfortable, supported postures reduce unwanted muscle activity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Good standing posture is best described as:

options.C: Any position held for one minute
options.D: The position in which the least muscular effort is needed to maintain body alignment

questions.explanation: Good posture minimises stress on joints and ligaments and uses minimal muscular energy.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A ‘round back’ (thoracic kyphosis) posture is typically associated with:

options.C: Tight pectoral muscles and weak scapular retractors and thoracic extensors

questions.explanation: Upper crossed syndrome (Janda): tight pectorals and upper trapezius with weak deep neck flexors and lower trapezius.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Coordination exercises such as Frenkel's are based on the principle of:

options.B: Repetition of controlled movements with visual feedback

questions.explanation: They re-educate smooth, accurate movement in ataxia by progressively increasing complexity.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The hip strategy for balance recovery is typically used when:

options.B: Perturbation is large or the support surface is narrow, requiring rapid movement at the hips
options.D: A small slow sway is controlled at the ankle

questions.explanation: Ankle strategy handles small perturbations on firm ground; hip strategy is for larger/faster ones; stepping strategy for the largest.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The correct handgrip height of an axillary crutch is such that the elbow is flexed about:
questions.explanation: Check at the greater trochanter or the wrist crease; the axillary pad is 4–5 cm below the axilla to prevent crutch palsy.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Pressure of an axillary crutch pad in the axilla can cause injury to the:
questions.explanation: Crutch palsy affects the radial nerve (wrist drop); weight must be borne through the hands.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A patient with a fracture who must not put any weight on one leg would use which crutch gait?

options.B: Swing-through gait with both legs weight-bearing

questions.explanation: Three-point: both crutches and the affected leg forward together, then the sound leg.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The four-point crutch gait is the sequence:

options.A: Right crutch and left foot together then the opposite
options.C: Both crutches together then both feet
options.D: Right crutch, left foot, left crutch, right foot

questions.explanation: It is the slowest but most stable gait, used in bilateral weakness or poor balance.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: When climbing stairs with crutches, the correct sequence is:

options.A: Up with the bad, down with the good
options.C: Up with the good, down with the bad

questions.explanation: Going up the stronger leg leads, then crutches and weaker leg; going down the crutches and weaker leg lead.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A single-point cane should be held:

options.A: In the hand on the same side as the affected limb
options.B: In either hand with no difference
options.D: In the hand opposite the affected lower limb

questions.explanation: The cane moves with the affected leg and reduces the load on it through the contralateral arm.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which walking aid provides the greatest base of support and stability?
questions.explanation: A walker supports up to 50% of body weight and is used when balance is poor.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In a wheelchair for a patient with bilateral lower limb amputations the rear axle should be moved:
questions.explanation: Loss of leg weight shifts the centre of gravity posteriorly, so the axle must be moved back to prevent tipping.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A patient finds it easier to walk in water mainly because of:
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle: an immersed body experiences an upthrust equal to the weight of water displaced, reducing weight bearing.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: When a patient is immersed to the level of the C7 spinous process, the percentage of body weight borne is about:
questions.explanation: Weight bearing: chest 25–35%, waist 50%, symphysis pubis 50–60%; C7 ~8–10%.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Water gives resistance to movement mainly because of its:
questions.explanation: Resistance increases with speed and surface area; allows speed-dependent strengthening.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Hydrostatic pressure on a limb immersed in water helps to:

options.A: Reduce oedema and increase venous return
options.C: Decrease heart rate and venous return

questions.explanation: Pressure increases with depth and acts equally on all surfaces.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which condition is a contraindication to hydrotherapy?

options.B: Open infected wounds, uncontrolled epilepsy or bowel incontinence

questions.explanation: Infection control and safety are crucial; also unstable cardiac status and fever.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which aquatic activity is MOST effective in reducing tone in a patient with spasticity?

options.C: Slow, passive movements with the patient floating supported in warm water

questions.explanation: Warm water, buoyancy and slow rhythmic movements relax muscles; speed and cold increase tone.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In suspension therapy using a fixed point suspension, the point of suspension is placed:

options.A: At the end of the limb
options.B: Above the patient's head regardless of joint
options.D: Directly above the axis of the joint being exercised

questions.explanation: When the fixed point lies over the joint axis, the limb swings in a horizontal plane with gravity eliminated.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In effleurage, the hands move:

options.A: In the direction of venous and lymphatic flow towards the heart

questions.explanation: Effleurage is stroking used to start and finish massage; deep effleurage aids venous return.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Kneading, wringing and rolling are all variations of:
questions.explanation: Petrissage is compression of muscle to improve circulation and release adhesions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Hacking, clapping, cupping and beating are movements of:
questions.explanation: Percussion stimulates tissue and is used in chest physiotherapy to loosen secretions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In deep transverse friction massage (Cyriax) the therapist:

options.A: Slides along the skin using oil
options.D: Moves the tissue back and forth perpendicular to the direction of the fibres without sliding on the skin

questions.explanation: No lubricant is used so that the skin moves with the fingers and the deep tissue is mobilised; used in tendinitis and ligament sprains.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Massage is contraindicated over:

options.A: A deep vein thrombosis, acute inflammation or malignancy

questions.explanation: Massage may dislodge thrombus or spread infection and tumour cells.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: During the acute stage of myositis ossificans, which treatment is contraindicated?

options.D: Active-assisted range of movement within pain limits

questions.explanation: Massage and passive stretching can worsen bleeding and promote heterotopic ossification.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which receptor is most sensitive to vibration, deep pressure and rapid changes in joint position?
questions.explanation: Pacinian corpuscles are rapidly adapting receptors; Ruffini endings sense sustained pressure and joint position.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The muscle spindle is sensitive to:

options.C: Changes in muscle length and the rate of change

questions.explanation: Intrafusal fibres detect stretch and trigger the stretch reflex; Golgi tendon organs sense tension.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Golgi tendon organ responds to:

options.A: Tension in the muscle-tendon unit and causes autogenic inhibition

questions.explanation: Excess tension excites the GTO, inhibiting the homonymous muscle through inhibitory interneurons.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Reciprocal inhibition means that contraction of an agonist:

options.C: Has no effect on the antagonist

questions.explanation: Basis of agonist-contract stretching techniques.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Slow-twitch (type I) muscle fibres are characterised by:

options.D: High oxidative capacity, fatigue resistance and postural function

questions.explanation: Type I: red, slow, aerobic; type IIb: white, fast, glycolytic, fatigable.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Aerobic training mainly improves:

options.C: Maximal oxygen uptake (VO2 max) and cardiovascular endurance

questions.explanation: Training adaptations include increased stroke volume, capillary density and mitochondrial enzymes.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The FITT principle in exercise prescription stands for:
questions.explanation: Prescribe frequency (days/week), intensity (% HRmax or 1-RM), time (duration) and type of exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The primary purpose of a cool-down after exercise is to:

options.B: Gradually reduce heart rate and prevent venous pooling or hypotension

questions.explanation: A cool-down helps remove metabolic waste and avoids blood pooling in the legs.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A proper warm-up before exercise helps by:

options.D: Increasing muscle temperature, blood flow and joint lubrication

questions.explanation: 5–10 minutes of low-intensity activity increases nerve conduction and prepares muscles for loading.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The main benefit of continuous passive motion (CPM) after ligament reconstruction is:

options.C: Reduction of joint stiffness and adhesion formation

questions.explanation: CPM is an adjunct that maintains mobility and nutrition of cartilage; it does not replace active exercise.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Joint play movements are:

options.A: Small involuntary accessory movements within the joint that cannot be performed actively

questions.explanation: Roll, glide and spin occur passively and are essential for full range of motion (Mennell).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which statement best differentiates mobilisation from manipulation?

options.C: Mobilisation is performed only under anaesthetic
options.D: Mobilisation is a graded passive technique the patient can resist; manipulation is a high-velocity thrust at the end range

questions.explanation: In mobilisation the patient can stop the movement; manipulation is a small-amplitude thrust beyond the elastic barrier.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The movement a patient can perform unaided through the joint's range is called:
questions.explanation: Active ROM depends on muscle strength and joint mobility; passive ROM is usually larger.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: If a patient's active range is less than passive range at the knee, the most likely cause is:
questions.explanation: When PROM is greater than AROM the limitation is in the contractile unit; when both are equally limited the joint structures are restricted.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Which is the first functional task usually taught to a patient with a thoracic spinal cord injury?
questions.explanation: Bed mobility, then sitting balance, transfers, wheelchair skills and later gait.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: After a total hip replacement via the posterior approach, the use of an abduction pillow:

options.A: Prevents adduction and dislocation of the prosthesis in bed
options.C: Is used only for the knee

questions.explanation: Keep the legs separated while lying and sleeping.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
